findings.reason: as written the section's first clause delivers nothing new and its negative control ("a planted disagreement turns it red") already passes today, so the section must be restated as extending this test rather than adding one.
findings.text: §3 states "the ISN version is pinned in two places in pyproject.toml" and asks for "a default-tier test [that] fails when the two pyproject pins disagree with each other", but `test_isn_requirements_agree_on_one_exact_version` at tests/core/test_isn_pin_agreement.py:36 already collects every `imas-standard-names` requirement from pyproject.toml and asserts they name one exact version (`assert len(versions) == 1`, line 50), with `assert len(requirements) >= 2` at line 44 forcing both pins to be present — the described guard already exists and already passes at head, so what §3 actually needs is the two comparisons it lacks (the installed package's version, pyproject.toml:81-83's `version("imas-standard-names")`, and the active grammar snapshot's version in imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_sync.py:288-332) added to this file

findings.reason: the section must say it extends the existing PR-opening branch and reuses those body helpers, otherwise a node will write a third body builder that drifts from the two that exist.
findings.text: §4 asks that a whole-catalog candidate "open the same kind of review request on the fork", but `run_release` already builds and opens a pull request through the injected `pr_creator` at catalog_release.py:1419-1431 when `final=True`, and `run_review_release` does the same at catalog_release.py:2250-2262 with full markdown-linked bodies (`body_with_exclusion_ledger_link` at :250, `body_with_export_report_link` at :294, `_write_and_verify_review_preview_link` at :161, `backfill_review_artifact` at :1634); the RC branch simply falls past `if final:` at :1341 and goes to the tag path at :1431 — so §4 is an extension of one branch in that function, and §4's "body uses markdown links rather than bare URLs" is already satisfied by the helpers named above while the inline body at :1414-1417 carries a bare ` {git_tag}` in backticks and no link ; its second clause, "the same run against an upstream remote refuses before any push", is likewise already implemented — `_check_final_targets_upstream` at imas_codex/cli/release.py:437 raises unless the remote owner is `iterorganization`, and it is called at imas_codex/cli/release.py:1401 under `if final:` — so both halves of §4's done-when are a condition change on machinery that exists, one in `run_release` and one in the CLI pre-flight

findings.reason: the honest change is to reuse the helpers, and a plan that does not say so invites a parallel body builder with its own untested refusal paths.
findings.text: a whole-catalog PR body built inside `run_release` would be a thin layer over machinery `run_review_release` already exercises: the exclusion-ledger link, the export-report link and the preview-link invariant at :161 are each a separately-tested helper with their own refusal exception classes (`ExclusionLedgerLinkError` :50, `ExportReportLinkError` :54, `ReviewPreviewLinkInvariantError` :46), and the existing inline body at :1414-1417 proves what happens without them (a body with no link at all); the design should route the RC path through the same helpers and state why the branch differs rather than why it is parallel

findings.reason: a forked endpoint checker will not be wired into the schema-compliance run and will drift from the type check that already covers the same edges, leaving the declared pair unenforced the moment either changes.
findings.text: §2 requires "a graph check that compares each CORRECTS edge's endpoint labels with the declared pair, added where none exists", and names no owner; the repository already owns two adjacent checks: `cypher_property_check.py` parses Cypher with `NODE_BINDING_RE` (:15) and validates bound properties against the LinkML schema with a frozen adjudication table (`_ADJUDICATED_OCCURRENCES` :66), and `tests/graph/test_schema_compliance.py:41` compares the graph's relationship *types* against `EXPECTED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES` (derived from `RELATIONSHIPS`, imas_codex/graph/schema_context_data.py:2294, whose tuples already carry both endpoint labels and cardinality); the endpoint comparison belongs as a second assertion in one of those two, not as a new checker, and the declaration belongs beside the existing `relationship_type` slots in imas_codex/schemas/standard_name.yaml:997 onward

findings.reason: naming the existing guards and the ancestry idiom turns §5 from "measure whether a cut works" into a bounded change to one predicate plus its test, and a forked precondition would leave two different definitions of "safe revision" in the same function.
findings.text: §5 asks for a release to run from a detached worktree and for "the guard that stops a release cut from an unmerged revision still fires"; the release path already owns three precondition mechanisms in this one file — `_check_on_main` (:802) reading `git branch --show-current`, `_check_clean_tree` (:812), `_check_synced` (:864), and an ancestry test `merge-base --is-ancestor old_head base_ref` at :474 inside `_prepare_release_branch` — so a detached worktree is refused by :803-807 because `--show-current` prints nothing there, and the fix is to let that guard accept a detached head proven merged by the ancestry idiom already at :474, not to add a worktree-specific precondition beside it — and the census of that type is **two owners, not one**: `_check_on_main` is implemented a second time at imas_codex/cli/release.py:321 (its own `subprocess.run(["git","branch","--show-current"])`, raising `click.ClickException`) and is called at imas_codex/cli/release.py:1398, so a node that repairs only catalog_release.py:802 leaves the CLI guard refusing every detached-worktree cut and §5's endpoint unreached; the duplication extends to the sibling preconditions `_check_clean_tree` (:812) and `_check_synced` (:864), each mirrored in the CLI pre-flight at :1400-1401

findings.reason: the section under-states its census by at least four sites and its reuse clause is unimplementable as stated against the existing rule, so a node following it would either break the sibling rule or fork a second boundary test.
findings.text: §8's done-when says "the import-boundary test covers the package's top-level modules as well as its subpackages", but that test's rule is `PACKAGES = ("graph_store", "worker_tasks")` (:17) with `test_package_imports_only_shared_module` forbidding *every* sibling import inside a package (:52, `assert not forbidden, ... "forbidden sibling imports"`); applied to the top-level modules that same rule forbids all cross-module imports, so the endpoint needs a second rule (private-name imports only) living in this one test file, and §8 states no such distinction; my own census of `imas_codex/standard_names/*.py` (ast walk over absolute, level-1 and level-2 ImportFrom) finds **31 private cross-module names across 24 statements**, not the 27 the plan reports, including catalog_reconcile.py:31 (`catalog_import._normalize_field`), benchmark_roles.py:631, edit.py:98, harmonize.py:40, promote.py:1990, protection.py:185 (two names), provenance_lifecycle.py:27, provenance_rebuild.py:265 and signed_manifest.py:7311 (three names) — none of which the plan's enumeration mentions

findings.reason: at a budget of 0 across all four families a section that adds exported names must say in its own text what it retires or why nothing can be, and this one adds at least six without accounting for any.
findings.text: with the supplied week figures public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, §8's stated closure route is "through a public name the owning module exports" for each of the 24 statements it closes, so the section adds public definitions (`_base_token`, `_load_rules`, `_synonym_matches`, `_github_slug`, `_run_git`, `_contest` and the rest) to the package's surface, while §2 adds a declared relationship type to the generated models, and neither section names any public name, CLI option, MCP view or refusal a change retires, merges or explains as unreducible

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §8 would extend the existing boundary test's single "no sibling imports" rule to top-level modules, where that rule cannot hold; the endpoint needs one deeper rule inside that test, not a second test module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's endpoint-label check duplicates the Cypher-against-LinkML scan owned by imas_codex/graph/cypher_property_check.py and the relationship-type check in tests/graph/test_schema_compliance.py; §5's worktree support forked from the branch/ancestry guards already in catalog_release.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 adds public exports ("a public name the owning module exports") and §2 adds a declared relationship type, and §8 names nothing it retires or merges and §2 names no surface it removes, so neither accounts for its added surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3's pin test already exists as tests/core/test_isn_pin_agreement.py, and §4 would add a third pull-request path beside the two already in imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's new PR body for a whole-catalog candidate would re-derive links the existing helpers already build, rather than extending the shared PR-opening path.
